previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted due to dyspnea, diaphoresis, and a new first-degree atrioventricular block, with concern for cardiac and renal complications. He had a recent rise in creatinine and hyperkalemia, which resolved with IV fluids. A chest X-ray showed findings concerning for left lung pneumonia, prompting treatment with levofloxacin. The AV block was attributed to diltiazem, which was held and later restarted at a reduced dose with improvement. His rhythm was evaluated by electrophysiology and deemed stable. He remained on vancomycin to prevent C. diff recurrence during antibiotic treatment. His multiple myeloma and related pancytopenia were monitored without intervention. He improved clinically, with normalization of kidney function and stable vital signs, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for cardiology and continuation of antibiotics.
